title: feat: add structured managed-agent Responses output
author: karanray06
pr_body_excerpt:
- Builds on merged prerequisites #14479 (single-API registration) and #14491 (Workers runtime tests); no registration or migration changes in this PR.
- Adds ordered assistant/MCP output, lifecycle SSE events, and stateless history replay; preserves Chat tool results and media links through the shared adapter.
- Keeps reasoning effort; rejects unsupported managed-agent reasoning summaries with HTTP 400.
- Preserves strict usage validation and per-child billing. Staging verified Responses/Chat JSON+SSE, MCP/replay, implicit/explicit/system-prompt caching, OpenRouter, and 18 usage fault/control probes. Wallet debit exactly matched 25 charges (0.02658924 Pollen); all 14 failed calls were unbilled and managed wrappers cost zero.
- Latest main integrated; CI green. Staging migration/rollback rehearsed and all temporary resources removed. Two Mistral probes hit upstream rate limits; Gemini/OpenRouter passed. A pre-existing staging agent with obsolete connected-apps configuration remains unrelated. Production deployment is separate.

Fixes #14243

gist.headline: Agents, neatly arranged
gist.blurb: Managed agents now leave a properly ordered trail: assistant output, MCP calls, lifecycle events, and history all land where they should. Even the receipts survived the trip, which is unusually civilized for a distributed system.
gist.summary: Added structured managed-agent output to the Responses API, including ordered assistant and MCP results, lifecycle SSE events, stateless history replay, preserved Chat tool/media results, and HTTP 400 validation for unsupported reasoning summaries.
gist.impact: Developers can now run managed agents through Responses or Chat and reliably consume replayable JSON/SSE output, MCP activity, media links, strict usage data, and per-child billing without wrapper charges.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy agent-runtime garden where outputs travel in a clearly ordered path: assistant messages as glowing letter tiles, MCP tool results as small labeled parcels, and SSE lifecycle sparks flowing through a retro terminal. Polli acts as the calm coordinator with a tiny clipboard, while the eager monitor robot watches the ordered event stream and code-plants grow from the validated usage receipts.
